items.stem: Why can a model score highly on a public benchmark yet fail in production?

options.text: The benchmark may not represent the real distribution, or be contaminated
options.rationale: Correct: benchmark gains need not transfer to the production population.
Accuracy is sometimes appropriate; the issue is representativeness.
Production has data; the mismatch is distributional.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce data leakage in evaluation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Split time-series data by time rather than randomly
options.rationale: Correct: random shuffling lets future rows leak into training.

options.text: Fit preprocessing on the training split only
options.rationale: Correct: fitting on all data leaks test information.

options.text: Tune hyperparameters on the test set
options.rationale: This leaks the test set into model selection.

options.text: Copy some test rows into training
options.rationale: This is direct leakage and inflates scores.

items.explanation: Correct: random shuffling lets future rows leak into training.

items.stem: For a highly imbalanced fraud dataset, which metric is most informative?

options.rationale: Correct: PR curves focus on the rare positive class.
Accuracy is dominated by the majority class and can be misleading.
Dataset size is not a performance metric.
Speed is not a quality metric.

items.explanation: Correct: PR curves focus on the rare positive class.
